title: How It Felt, What I Hope

lessons.title: كنت سعيدا (kuntu saʿīdan) — I was happy
lessons.gloss: I was happy — a feeling in the past: kāna hands its description the -an of the accusative, and shaʿartu bi- names the feeling as a noun

segments.text: Say "I missed the train", then "who is in charge here?". (Fātanī al-qiṭār, man al-masʾūl hunā?)
A story of a trip is not finished until you say how it felt.
Today needs no verb: anā saʿīd, I'm happy. In the past kāna comes in, and the word that describes takes -an, the accusative:
كنت سعيدا. — kuntu saʿīdan — I was happy.
كانت حزينة. — kānat ḥazīna — She was sad.

On most words the -an is written with a final ا: سعيدا, متعبا, غاضبا. On a word ending in ة it is not written, and at the end of a sentence it is not said: kānat ḥazīna. You met it already in kuntu mutʿaban and kāna aṭ-ṭaqs jamīlan.
To name the feeling as a noun, say shaʿartu bi-, "I felt", with the feeling after bi-:
شعرت بالخوف عندما طارت الطائرة. — shaʿartu bi-l-khawf ʿindamā ṭārat aṭ-ṭāʾira — I felt afraid when the plane took off.
Word for word, "I felt fear". Aḥsastu bi-, from aḥassa, to feel, says the same: aḥsastu bi-l-khawf.

segments.instruction: "I'm happy", then "I was happy" — anā saʿīd, kuntu saʿīdan
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "I'm happy", then "I was happy" — *anā saʿīd*, *kuntu saʿīdan*]

segments.instruction: "I felt afraid when the plane took off" — shaʿartu bi-l-khawf ʿindamā ṭārat aṭ-ṭāʾira
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "I felt afraid when the plane took off" — *shaʿartu bi-l-khawf ʿindamā ṭārat aṭ-ṭāʾira*]

segments.instruction: a feeling and what came of it — kuntu ghāḍiban, fa-kharajtu
segments.source: [YOU SAY: a feeling and what came of it — *kuntu ghāḍiban, fa-kharajtu*]

segments.text: "I was happy"? (Kuntu saʿīdan, with -an.) Why the -an? (Kāna gives it to the word that describes.) "I felt afraid"? (Shaʿartu bi-l-khawf.)

lessons.title: تجربة (tajriba) — an experience
lessons.gloss: an experience; a try, an experiment — something you went through and learned from

segments.text: Say "I was happy", then "I felt afraid". (Kuntu saʿīdan, shaʿartu bi-l-khawf.)
You have a verb for trying on a coat, jarraba. Its noun covers much more than coats.
تجربة — tajriba — "an experience"; also "a try, an experiment".
كانت الرحلة تجربة (tajriba) جديدة. — kānat ar-riḥla tajribatan jadīda — The trip was a new experience.
It is kāna's -an again: tajribatan, though the ة hides it on the page. Tajriba mumtiʿa is an enjoyable experience; tajriba mumilla, a boring one.

تجربة (tajriba) is built on the native Arabic root j-r-b, "to try, to test" (Lane). Lane gives jarraba as making trial of a thing, time after time, and tajriba as its noun: a trial. An experience, in Arabic, is something you have tried.

segments.instruction: "The trip was a new experience" — kānat ar-riḥla tajribatan jadīda
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "The trip was a new experience" — *kānat ar-riḥla tajribatan jadīda*]

segments.instruction: "an enjoyable experience", then "a boring one" — tajriba mumtiʿa, tajriba mumilla
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "an enjoyable experience", then "a boring one" — *tajriba mumtiʿa*, *tajriba mumilla*]

segments.instruction: "In my opinion it was a good experience" — fī raʾyī kānat tajribatan jayyida
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "In my opinion it was a good experience" — *fī raʾyī kānat tajribatan jayyida*]

segments.text: What does تجربة (tajriba) mean? ("An experience; a try".) Which verb shares its root? (Jarraba, to try.) "A new experience"? (Tajriba jadīda.)

lessons.title: أتمنى أن (atamannā an) — I hope to
lessons.gloss: I hope to, I wish to — atamannā an and aḥlumu bi- for hopes and dreams, and urīdu an uṣbiḥa for what you want to become

segments.text: Say "the trip was a new experience". (Kānat ar-riḥla tajribatan jadīda.) Then "I felt afraid". (Shaʿartu bi-l-khawf.)
That was the past. Now turn ahead: what you hope for, what you dream of, what you want to become.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: atamannā an, aḥlumu bi-

segments.text: Tamannā, to wish, from chapter one hundred and fourteen, has the present atamannā, I hope, I wish. An and the subjunctive follow it, as after urīdu:
أتمنى أن أجد وظيفة جديدة. — atamannā an ajida waẓīfa jadīda — I hope to find a new job.
Ajida is the subjunctive of ajidu, I find, from wajada; the w has dropped again.
For a dream, use the verb of ḥulm: aḥlumu bi-, I dream of, with a noun after bi-: aḥlumu bi-riḥla ṭawīla, I dream of a long journey.

blocks.title: Grammar Lens: what you want to become

segments.text: Aṣbaḥa, to become, behaves like kāna: what it becomes takes -an.
أريد أن أصبح مهندسا. — urīdu an uṣbiḥa muhandisan — I want to become an engineer.
Uṣbiḥa is its subjunctive, after an. In the past: aṣbaḥtu muhandisan, I became an engineer.

segments.instruction: "I hope to find a new job" — atamannā an ajida waẓīfa jadīda
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "I hope to find a new job" — *atamannā an ajida waẓīfa jadīda*]

segments.instruction: "I dream of a long journey" — aḥlumu bi-riḥla ṭawīla
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "I dream of a long journey" — *aḥlumu bi-riḥla ṭawīla*]

segments.instruction: "I want to become an engineer" — urīdu an uṣbiḥa muhandisan
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "I want to become an engineer" — *urīdu an uṣbiḥa muhandisan*]

segments.instruction: "She wants to become a doctor" — turīdu an tuṣbiḥa ṭabība
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "She wants to become a doctor" — *turīdu an tuṣbiḥa ṭabība*]

segments.instruction: your own: atamannā an and one thing, then urīdu an uṣbiḥa and one job
segments.source: [YOU SAY: your own: *atamannā an* and one thing, then *urīdu an uṣbiḥa* and one job]

segments.text: "I hope to"? (Atamannā an.) "I dream of"? (Aḥlumu bi-.) "To become", after an? (Uṣbiḥa.) What does aṣbaḥa give the word after it? (The -an, as kāna does.)

lessons.title: Review — how it felt, and what comes next
lessons.gloss: how it felt and what you hope for — kuntu saʿīdan, shaʿartu bi-, tajriba, atamannā an, aḥlumu bi- and urīdu an uṣbiḥa

segments.text: Buy a return ticket and ask the price. (Tadhkirat dhahāb wa-iyāb, min faḍlik. Bi-kam at-tadhkira?) Then report a problem and ask for the person in charge. (Fātanī al-qiṭār. Urīdu an atakallama maʿa al-masʾūl.)

Three lessons, and an experience can be told from both ends. Looking back: kuntu saʿīdan, kānat ḥazīna, shaʿartu bi-l-khawf, kānat tajribatan jadīda. Looking ahead: atamannā an, aḥlumu bi-, urīdu an uṣbiḥa.
Both ends in one breath:
كانت تجربة (tajriba) صعبة، لكن أتمنى أن أسافر قريبا. — kānat tajribatan ṣaʿba, lākin atamannā an usāfira qarīban — It was a hard experience, but I hope to travel again soon.

segments.instruction: "He wants to become an actor" — yurīdu an yuṣbiḥa mumaththilan
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "He wants to become an actor" — *yurīdu an yuṣbiḥa mumaththilan*]

segments.instruction: "The barber was angry" — kāna al-ḥallāq ghāḍiban
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "The barber was angry" — *kāna al-ḥallāq ghāḍiban*]

segments.instruction: "I told my grandmother how the trip was" — ḥakaytu li-jaddatī kayfa kānat ar-riḥla
segments.source: [YOU SAY: "I told my grandmother how the trip was" — *ḥakaytu li-jaddatī kayfa kānat ar-riḥla*]

segments.instruction: how your last trip felt, and one thing you hope for next time
segments.source: [YOU SAY: how your last trip felt, and one thing you hope for next time]

segments.text: "I was tired"? (Kuntu mutʿaban.) "I felt afraid"? (Shaʿartu bi-l-khawf.) "I hope to travel"? (Atamannā an usāfira.) "An experience"? (Tajriba.)
